# 【Standard WEB Ticket Sale】Mark Your Calendar and Let’s Go!

2026.03.13

Thank you for traveling with us!

Standard WEB Ticket for April and May will be on sale from 3pm on March 13 onwards.

Please see the sales details as below.

**Standard WEB Ticket Details**

**１．Sales Schedule**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/3e3bd53c01148d1be6ae465d42720ca4.png)

\*Sales schedule for June onwards will be announced when we have details, so stay tuned! Tickets will be on sale usually one month before.

\*The sales schedule is current as of March 13, 2026.

\*Please note that it may be subject to change.

\*We will inform you of the schedule from November 4th onwards at a later date.

**2\. Traveling Sections**

[WEB Ticket Reservation Traveling Sections](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/yoyakuweb_kukan)

The last express bus from Ogizawa Station to Nagano Station departs Ogizawa Station at 17:00. Passengers traveling to Nagano should pay attention to the connection time.

**3\. Fare**

Normal fare will be applied to this WEB Ticket and option ticket.

[Fares for individual customers (1-14 people)](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/transport/fare.html)

If you wish to take an express train between Dentetsu Toyama and Tateyama, you will need to pay an additional express fare.

Express fare have changed from April 1st, please visit [“Regarding the Operation of Rapid limited express trains and Revisions to Limited Express Fares”](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/train-express-fares)

**4\. How to Purchase**

This ticket can be purchased only on [WEB Ticket Page](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html).

\*Cannot be purchased at a ticket counter.

**5\. Others**

[<WEB Ticket> How to Change or Cancel Your Reservation](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_change_and_cancellation)

\*Sales period for June onwards will be anounced when we have details.

**\*Please refrain from making reservations through travel agencies.**

Have an easy, convenient trip with WEB Tickets!

We look forward to your booking! [WEB Ticket Page](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html)

## Item Information

### Train Eco WEB Ticket

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3853e08e62e5f84019f1dde6aa4d0100.jpg)

【Only for residents of Japan】

Available only on specific sections.

Enjoy eco-friendly transportations and get discounts at shops and restaurants along Alpine Route.

**for more detail**

### Early Bird Discount WEB ticket

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/89899ac15f3b401ea30d2586d79957a8.jpg)

It is 10day before advance early bird web ticket for recommended section.

It can be used by both day-tripper and those staying overnight within Alpine Route.

【Important】. You need to make a reservation at least 10days in advance, and the cancellation fee is 1,000JPY.

**The winter schedule for boarding times applies from November 4 to November 10.**

**for more detail**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/00b3f7012b1176968f0fbb01a1d57d01.jpg)

**Only for the guests staying within Alpine Route (Murodo/Midagahara/Tengudaira) who are departing after 2:00PM**

【Important】This item's conditions are partially different from the standard "WEB Ticket'". You need to make a reservation at least 10days in advance, and the cancellation fee is 1,000JPY.

**for more detail**

This web ticket guarantees seating on the Toyama Chihō Railway between Dentetsu Toyama and Tateyama Stations.

This is a web ticket guaranteeing a seat on the Toyama Chihō Railway train ”Canyon Express”or "Double Decker Express" departing Dentetsu Toyama at 8:20 am bound for Tateyama Station.

**for more detail**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/936438bb632d8267fe426271579c6520.jpg)

It is a standard ticket that can be reserved for all season.

You can reserve it up until 3:00 PM the day before.

**It can be used by both day-tripper and those staying overnight within Alpine Route**

**The winter schedule for boarding times applies from November 4 to November 10.**

**for more detail**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/05284c017a4169b50503d25a00632f61.jpg)

It is a standard ticket that can be reserved for all season.

You can reserve it up until 3:00 PM the day before.

**Only for the guests staying within Alpine Route (Murodo/Midagahara/Tengudaira) who are departing after 2:00PM**

**for more detail**

![](http://www.alpen-route.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/6e65701c83c2ae587a92cfa9c2411333.jpg)

We will operate a limited-time direct bus service from Tateyama Station to Murodo without any transfers.

**for more detail**

**【Only for residents of Japan】**

**Including the Toyama Chihou Railway section, “Train Eco WEB Ticket” will provide you some benefits.**

**As a purchase benefit, you can get a 5% discount at Alpine Route souvenir shops and restaurants.**

**\*The number of these tickets is limited and sold for designated traveling sections only.**

**【IMPORTANT】**

**・This product is only for residents of Japan.**

**・Cancellation fee of 500JPY/person will be applied if you cancel after 11:59 PM 10 days prior to your departure date.**

**・Please check the details prior to purchase.**

**２. Sales Period & Usage Period**

**| --- | --- |**
**| August 8 - August 16 | 10AM on June 26 |**
**| September 19 - September 23 | 10AM on Augsut 3 |**

**\*Sections except the designated section as stated above cannot be purchased.**

**\*Tickets (Tateyama Station - Kurobeko) are valid for 5 days.**

**【IMPORTANT】**

**\*We cannot accept customer request for a refund after you receive your tickets.**

**４. Purchase Benefit**

**Get a 5% discount at Alpen Route souvenir shops and restaurants!**

**\*Please show your ticket at designated facilities.**

**≪Designated Facilities≫**

**Restaurant Tateyama(Murodo Terminal),Tea Lounge Rindo(Murodo Terminal),Murodo Souvenir Shop(1F&2F),Kurobedaira Souvenir Shop,and Tateyama Station souvenir Shop”TATEYAMA ALPEN STORE”※Excluding Montbell Tateyama Station Store**

**６. Others**

**Child：　￥５,４８０　→　　￥４,９５０**

The express bus between "Ogizawa and Nagano" and the local bus between "Ogizawa and Shinano Omachi" do not offer a specific boarding time. Please refer to [**here**](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/timetable/) for the timetable of limited express bus and local bus.

Refunds for reductions in the number of passengers or section changes on the day of use will be accepted at the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route departure stations (Dentetsu Toyama and Tateyama Stations for passengers coming from Toyama Prefecture, or Ogizawa for passengers coming from Nagano Prefecture). (Option Ticket Change fee: 100 yen per person, one way. Please note that no refunds will be made for reasons other than a reduction in the number of passengers or a change in section.

**If you are traveling from the Nagano Prefecture side (Nagano, Shinano-Omachi), you can take the express bus and the local bus without a ticket. Please hand over your smartphone with your reservation information or a piece of paper with your reservation information to the bus driver when you use the bus.**

## Tateyama Kurobe Passes, Tickets, and Transportation Fees

Visiting Tateyama Kurobe does not require an entrance ticket, but you need to purchase tickets to ride the transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. You can purchase tickets for a single mode of transportation, such as the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira, or you can purchase a pass for all transportation on a specific route, such as a pass from Tateyama Station to Ogizawa Station, which allows you to ride the Tateyama Cable Car, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Tunnel Trolley Bus, Tateyama Ropeway, Kurobe Cable Car, and Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus.

The price of a pass for a specific route is the sum of the fares for all transportation on that route, with no discount. However, if you purchase a round-trip ticket, there is a discount. For example, a one-way ticket from Tateyama Station to Kurobe Lake costs 9,140 yen, while a round-trip ticket costs 16,480 yen, which is about a 10% discount compared to two one-way tickets.

## How to Purchase Tickets for Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Transportation

The second method is to pre-purchase tickets through the official website of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route and then print the tickets at the self-service ticket machines at the station on the day or the day before. Below is a detailed explanation of these two methods.

### 2\. Purchasing Tickets in Advance on the Official Website

In addition to purchasing tickets upon arrival at the station, tickets for various transportation methods on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route can also be purchased through the official online ticketing system ( [Tateyama Kurobe Alpen Route WEB Ticket](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html)).

Among the various transportation methods on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, only the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam require reserved seating times. The Tateyama Cable Car from Bijodaira to Tateyama Station, the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Kurobe Dam to Ogizawa Station, and other transportation methods do not require reserved seating times.

Therefore, when touring the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, only one ride requires a reserved seating time. If you are ascending from Tateyama Station, the reserved seating time is for the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira. If you are ascending from Ogizawa Station, the reserved seating time is for the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.

Since more people ascend from Tateyama Station, the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira is generally more heavily booked, and the cable car has limited capacity. Therefore, on weekends and holidays during the peak season, it often gets fully booked early. On the other hand, fewer people ascend from Ogizawa Station, and the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus has a larger capacity, so there are usually seats available on the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.

If there are no available seats for online reservations, it does not necessarily mean that the ride is fully booked, as a portion of seats are reserved for on-the-spot sales on the day. Therefore, even if there are no seats available online, you may still be able to purchase tickets at the station on the day. Additionally, only regular rides are available for online booking, but during the peak season, there are usually extra rides that are not available for online booking, so you can generally purchase tickets for these at the station.

In summary, if you want to plan your trip more securely, you can purchase tickets and reserve seating times for the Tateyama Cable Car or Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus in advance online. However, even if you cannot reserve your desired time, there is no need to worry. Arriving early at the station (Toyama Station, Tateyama Station, or Ogizawa Station) on the day will allow you to purchase tickets and board the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route.

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select route](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-03.webp)

\[Step 5\] After setting the above options, images of the available products will appear. Click on the product image, then select the desired boarding time slot and the specific boarding time. (Note: The boarding time refers to the departure time for either the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam.)

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select boarding time](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-04.webp)

\[Step 6\] Specify the number of passengers. (Note: Individuals aged 12 or older need to purchase adult tickets (おとな（中学生以上）). Children aged 6-11 purchase child tickets (こども（小学生）). Children under 6 are free of charge and do not need to be selected in the passenger count.)

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - select number of passengers](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-05.webp)

\[Step 7\] Choose whether to add [bus tickets](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_op1-1) from Ogizawa Station to Shinano-Omachi Station or Nagano Station. Leave it blank if not needed. After making your selection, click “ご予約内容の確認” (Confirm Reservation Details).

![Tateyama Kurobe online ticket purchase - add-on tickets](https://www.travelclassroom.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/alpine-web-ticket-update-06.webp)

\[Note\]: Bus tickets purchased through the online ticket system for the [route bus between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi Station](https://www.alpico.co.jp/traffic/local/hakuba/ogizawa/) and the [express bus between Ogizawa Station and Nagano Station](https://www.alpico.co.jp/traffic/express/nagano_omachi/) cannot be refunded after purchase. However, the number of passengers can be reduced, but refunds can only be processed at the Ogizawa Station ticket office. When boarding the bus, you will need to present the electronic ticket from the online ticket system or a printed copy of the electronic ticket. For more details, please refer to [this webpage](https://www.alpen-route.com/_wp/webticket_op1-2). Additionally, bus tickets purchased here cannot be used for intermediate stops.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-13.jpg)

Note: The image above is from the official website tutorial.

[Klook.com](https://www.klook.com/)

\[Step 8\] After confirming that the ticket information is correct, click “Enter payment information” to proceed to payment.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-14.jpg)

\[Step 9\] Enter your credit card information, including the credit card number (Credit card number), expiration date (Expiration date), and security code (CSC). Then click “Confirm payment information” to complete the payment.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-15.jpg)

After successfully purchasing the ticket, the ticket information will be displayed, including a QR Code. You can scan this QR Code at the self-service ticket machine at the station to collect your ticket. You can print this page, save a screenshot on your phone, or log in to the online ticket system on your phone to display the QR Code when collecting your ticket.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-16.jpg)

Note: The image above is from the official website tutorial.

##### (3) Changing Tickets

After purchasing tickets online, the only content that can be changed online is the number of passengers. You can log in to the [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html) to change the number of passengers (increase or decrease the number) before 2:59 PM the day before the ticket date (Japan time).

If you increase the number of passengers, you will need to pay for the additional tickets. If you decrease the number of passengers, the refund for the reduced tickets will be credited back to the credit card used for the purchase. Changing the number of passengers through the online ticket system before the deadline does not incur a handling fee.

To change the number of passengers, log in to the online ticket system and go to My Page. Click on “Confirm reservation“, then click “Change” in the displayed ticket record to make changes.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-17.jpg)

After the deadline (2:59 PM the day before the ticket date), you cannot change the number of passengers through the online ticket system. However, if you have not yet collected the ticket, you can make changes at the ticket counter at the station (Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, or Dentetsu Toyama Station) on the day of travel. At the ticket counter, in addition to changing the number of passengers, you can also change the departure time (for the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam).

Even if the original departure time has passed, you can still make changes as long as the ticket has not been collected, but the new departure time must be on the same day as the original ticket. Changing the number of passengers or departure time at the station ticket counter incurs a handling fee of 500 yen per ticket.

Additionally, please note that bus tickets purchased through the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Online Ticket System for the route bus between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi Station and the express bus between Ogizawa Station and Nagano Station cannot be refunded. Refunds for reducing the number of passengers can only be processed at the Ogizawa Station ticket office.

##### (4) Canceling Tickets

Tickets for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route purchased online can be canceled through the [online ticketing system](https://tateyama-kurobe-webservice.jp/AlpenTour/html/VW001W0010.html). Cancellations made before 2:59 PM (Japan Time) on the day before the ticket date are free of charge. If canceled after this deadline but before the departure time (the Tateyama Cable Car from Tateyama Station to Bijodaira or the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus from Ogizawa Station to Kurobe Dam), a 500 yen fee per ticket will be charged. Cancellations are not possible after the departure time.

However, tickets purchased during the advance sale period, have special cancellation rules. If canceled 10 days before the travel date, no fee is charged. If canceled after this period, a 1,000 yen fee per ticket will be charged.

To cancel a ticket, log in to the online ticketing system, go to My Page, click on “Confirm reservation“, and then click “Cancel” on the displayed ticket record to proceed with the cancellation.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-18.jpg)

Note: The above image is from the official website tutorial.

##### 5\. Ticket Pickup

After purchasing Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets online, you need to collect the physical paper tickets before use. Tickets can be picked up from 12:00 PM (noon) on the day before the travel date. Physical tickets can be printed from self-service ticket machines at Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, and Toyama Station of the Toyama Chihou Railway. To print the ticket, simply scan the QR code from the ticket record on the machine and confirm on the screen to print the ticket.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-19.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-20.jpg)

Note: The above image is from the official website tutorial.

Below are the locations of the self-service ticket machines at Tateyama Station, Ogizawa Station, and Toyama Station of the Toyama Chihou Railway (official website tutorial images).

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-21.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-22.jpg)![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-web-ticket-23.jpg)

Self-service ticket machines are only available during station operating hours. The self-service ticket machines at Dentetsu Toyama Station can be used from 5:00 AM to 11:30 PM.

## Purchasing and Using JR Passes Including Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Tickets

In addition to purchasing individual tickets for the various transportation options on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, there are also several passes available that include transportation on the Alpine Route as well as JR trains and buses connecting nearby major cities.

Examples include the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass“, the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass“, and the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket“. If you are not driving to Tateyama Kurobe, purchasing these JR Passes or package tickets can generally save you a significant amount of money.

### 1\. Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass

The “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://touristpass.jp/en/alpine/)” is a JR Pass jointly offered by JR Central and JR West. This pass allows unlimited rides on the eight types of transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route during its validity period, as well as unlimited rides on JR trains between Nagoya and Toyama, and between Nagoya and Shinano-Omachi.

![Tateyama Kurobe JR Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/Alpine-JR-Pass_en.jpg)

The specific areas covered by the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass” include:

- JR trains between Nagoya and Toyama via the Tokaido Main Line (Nagoya to Gifu) and the Takayama Main Line, including limited express, express, rapid, and local trains (ordinary cars only, no Green Car). Stops include Gifu, Mino, Gero Onsen, Takayama, and Hida Furukawa.
- JR trains between Nagoya and Shinano-Omachi via the Chuo Main Line (Nagoya to Shiojiri), the Shinonoi Line (Shiojiri to Kitamatsumoto), and the Oito Line (Kitamatsumoto to Shinano-Omachi), including limited express, express, rapid, and local trains (ordinary cars only, no Green Car). Stops include Ena Gorge, Narai, and Matsumoto.
- Trains on the Toyama Chihou Railway between Toyama and Tateyama Station, including limited express, rapid, and local trains (non-reserved seats only).
- Route buses between Ogizawa Station and Shinano-Omachi, passing through Omachi Onsen.
- Six types of mountain transportation on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route between Tateyama Station and Ogizawa Station (Tateyama Cable Car, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Tunnel Trolleybus, Tateyama Ropeway, Kurobe Cable Car, and Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus).

For more detailed information on the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass”, please refer to the article “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass: Purchase, Exchange, Usage, and Riding Guide](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/alpine-pass.html)“.

### 2\. JR Central “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass”

The “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass](https://railway.jr-central.co.jp/tickets/tateyama-kurobe-alpine/)” is a domestic version for Japanese residents offered by JR Central, similar to the “ [Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/alpine-pass.html).”

The coverage area, validity period, and price of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass” are exactly the same as the “Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass,” but there are slight differences in the usage period, purchase period, sales channels, and how it is used.

Here are the basic details of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass“:

- Coverage: Exactly the same as the coverage of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Validity: 5 consecutive days, same as the validity of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Price: Adults 24,500 yen, Children 12,250 yen, same as the price of the Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass;
- Usage Period: April 15 to November 30, 2026, but not valid during April 27 – May 6 and August 10 – 19;
- Sales Period: March 15 to November 26, 2026. Tickets can only be purchased one month before the start date of use;
- Purchase Channel: [JR West’s “e5489” online booking site](https://tickets.jr-odekake.net/shohindb/view/consumer/tokutoku/ticket.html?staticShnId=100022957);
- Ticket Collection Method: At JR Central station ticket offices or at designated ticket vending machines marked “5489サービス” located outside the ticket gates.

Note: Before 2026, the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass” was called the “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Pass](https://jr-central.co.jp/news/release/_pdf/nws000001_00061.pdf).” It underwent a major revision starting in 2026.

Reference:

- [JR Central official website page for Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass](https://railway.jr-central.co.jp/tickets/tateyama-kurobe-alpine/)

For a detailed guide on the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass,” please refer to this article: [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Free Pass: How to Buy, Pick Up, and Ride](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/tateyama-kurobe-alpine-free-pass.html).

### 3\. “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket”

The “ [Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket](https://highway-buses.jp/ticket/alpineroute-shinjuku.php)” is a discount package for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route offered by Keio Dentetsu Bus.

The package includes a one-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo’s Shinjuku Station to Shinano-Omachi Station (or Ogizawa Station) in Nagano Prefecture, a route bus ticket from Shinano-Omachi Station to Ogizawa Station (included only in the daytime bus package), and one-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station.

These modes include the Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway.

![Tateyama Kurobe Ticket](https://www.travelclassroom.net/eng/wp-content/uploads/folder01/alpine-route-shinjuku-02.jpg)

The “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” is divided into two types, “Overnight Bus” and “Daytime Bus,” based on the departure time of the highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station.

For the “Overnight Bus” type, the highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station is an overnight sleeper bus. It departs at 11:15 PM and arrives at Ogizawa Station at 5:32 AM. You can start your mountain journey the same day, but you might be tired due to lack of sleep. Also, please note that the overnight highway bus from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station does not run every day, and according to the website information, the overnight bus is currently suspended.

For the “Daytime Bus” type, the highway bus runs during the day with 2 to 3 services daily. However, the daytime highway bus only goes as far as Shinano-Omachi. The journey takes about 4.5 hours, arriving in Shinano-Omachi in the afternoon or evening. To go from Shinano-Omachi to Ogizawa Station, you need to take a route bus. The package includes the ticket for the route bus from Shinano-Omachi to Ogizawa Station. This bus ticket is valid for two days, allowing you to get off midway, making it convenient to stay overnight in Shinano-Omachi or the nearby Omachi Onsen area before heading up the mountain.

Here are the tickets included in the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket”:

- Daytime Bus: One-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo Shinjuku Station to Shinano-Omachi Station (Nagano Prefecture) + Route bus ticket from Shinano-Omachi Station to Ogizawa Station (valid for 2 days, allowing boarding/alighting midway) + One-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station (Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway), valid for 5 days.
- Overnight Bus: One-way highway bus ticket from Tokyo Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station (Nagano Prefecture) + One-way tickets for the seven transportation modes on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Chihō Railway’s Toyama Station (Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus, Kurobe Cable Car, Tateyama Ropeway, Tateyama Tunnel Electric Bus, Tateyama Highland Bus, Tateyama Cable Car, and Toyama Chihō Railway), valid for 5 days.

The price for the “Daytime Bus” version of the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” is 19,000 yen (Children 9,500 yen). The “Overnight Bus” version is about 400 yen more expensive. The regular price for the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets from Ogizawa Station to Toyama Station is 12,170 yen, and the regular highway bus fare from Shinjuku Station to Ogizawa Station is 7,500 yen, totaling 19,670 yen. Therefore, purchasing the “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Shinjuku Ticket” saves you about 670 yen.

## **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets**

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Ticket](https://i0.wp.com/easytravelfollowme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2469-1.jpg?resize=640%2C480&ssl=1)Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket｜Photo by Tsubaki

The “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket” is the official transit pass for the Alpine Route.

![Transportation Map of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route](https://i0.wp.com/easytravelfollowme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-scaled.png?w=2560&ssl=1)Transportation Map of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route \| Source: Official Website

The entire route does **not** support IC cards (like Suica or Pasmo). You must purchase a Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket to ride the six different modes of transport between Tateyama Station and Ogizawa Station.

If you don’t plan to travel the full length, you can buy individual one-way tickets for specific segments (e.g., an electric bus ticket from Ogizawa to Kurobe Dam). However, having to go to the ticket window or machine at every single stop is extremely tedious.

Therefore, most people choose to buy a **one-way through ticket** or a **round-trip ticket** between Tateyama and Ogizawa. This saves the hassle of individual purchases, is slightly cheaper, and is much more convenient.

**Pro Tip:** If you are coming from the Kansai or Nagoya area, it is highly recommended to use the **[JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://easytravelfollowme.com/jr-pass/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)**. This pass allows unlimited free rides on all transportation within the Alpine Route (details below).

>\> Purchase online: \[ [JR Official Website](https://easytravelfollowme.com/jr-pass/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)\] \| \[ [KKday](https://easytravelfollowme.com/kkday/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)\]

The Alpine Route includes:

> ・ **Tateyama Cable Car**
>
> ・ **Tateyama Highland Bus**
>
> ・ **Tateyama Tunnel Trolley Bus**
>
> ・ **Kurobe Cable Car**
>
> ・ **Kurobe Ropeway**
>
> ・ **Kanden Tunnel Electric Bus**

If you’re still unsure how to get to Tateyama Kurobe or how these six vehicles work, I will cover them in **Chapter 3**. Stay tuned for the full explanation!

If you feel that planning a DIY trip to Tateyama Kurobe is too complicated, you can join one of the highly-rated **KKday tour groups**.

To be honest, if I weren’t self-driving with my boyfriend and were traveling solo instead, I would definitely choose a tour. Not only does it save a lot of trouble, but you can also travel safely with a guide without worrying about ticket availability.

### **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket: Basics and Precautions**

#### **One-Way or Round-Trip Options**

![Transportation Map of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Ticket](https://i0.wp.com/easytravelfollowme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-scaled.png?w=2560&ssl=1)Transportation Map of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route \| Source: Official Website

There are several common ways to use the **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket**.

> ・ **Tateyama Station** (Toyama side)
>
> ・ **Ogizawa Station** (Nagano side)

The most basic method is to start from either of the two entrances of the Alpine Route: **Tateyama Station (Toyama side)** on the left of the map, or **Ogizawa Station (Nagano side)** on the right. Your choice between a one-way through ticket or a round-trip ticket will depend on your travel itinerary.

If you are traveling by car like we did and plan to turn back midway (for example, starting from Ogizawa and only going as far as Murodo before returning), you can choose a **round-trip ticket**.

However, even if you are driving, you can still opt for a **one-way through ticket**. In this case, you can use a car forwarding service to have your vehicle driven to the other end of the Alpine Route. Please note that this service is not cheap, costing approximately **27,000 JPY per car**. If you are traveling in a large group, you might be able to split the cost.

\\* 27,000 JPY (≈ $175.50 USD / £129.87 GBP / €151.20 EUR)

#### **Purchasing Connecting Tickets**

If you are taking public transportation from major hubs like **Dentetsu Toyama Station** or **Nagano Station**, you can purchase “extension tickets” starting from these stations. This allows you to handle your entire journey with a single ticket, making connections much more convenient. (Refer to the price list below for details).

However, if you plan to rely primarily on public transport, you should consider the **[JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://easytravelfollowme.com/jr-pass/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)**, which is exclusive to foreign tourists.

A one-way trip from Nagano Station through the Alpine Route to Dentetsu Toyama Station costs at least **16,660 JPY**, not including the transportation costs to get to the region. It is often much more cost-effective to use this **24,000 JPY** **JR PASS**, which is valid for 5 days and allows you to visit other sightseeing spots along the way!

\\* 16,660 JPY (≈ $108.29 USD / £80.13 GBP / €93.30 EUR)\\* 24,000 JPY (≈ $156.00 USD / £115.44 GBP / €134.40 EUR)

> **JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass**
>
> **Validity:** 5 consecutive days
>
> **Price:** ¥24,000
>
> **Coverage:** Includes JR transportation in Nagoya, Matsumoto, and Takayama areas + full access to the Alpine Route.
>
> **Eligibility:** Limited to non-Japanese passport holders with “Temporary Visitor” status for sightseeing purposes.
>
> **>\> Purchase Online:** \[ [JR Pass Official Website](https://easytravelfollowme.com/jr-pass/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)\] \| \[ [KKday](https://easytravelfollowme.com/kkday/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)\] \| \[ [Klook](https://easytravelfollowme.com/klook/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)\]
>
> (Note: Discounts vary by period; it is recommended to compare prices across different platforms.)

#### **Departure from Tateyama or Ogizawa Requires a Reserved Time Slot**

The first leg of the journey from either end of the Alpine Route (Tateyama Station and Ogizawa Station) has limited seating and **fixed departure times**. You must board at your reserved time. When planning your itinerary, it is crucial to confirm your departure time first to ensure smooth connections for the rest of your trip or to coordinate your arrival from other attractions.

While subsequent transportation segments have schedules, they do not support reservations and operate on a first-come, first-served basis. This offers more flexibility, allowing you to spend more or less time at various scenic spots along the way.

>\> \[ [Click here to check the latest official timetable](https://www.alpen-route.com/en/timetable/)\]

#### **Validity: 5 Days (Not Unlimited Rides)**

A Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket allows you to travel each segment **only once**. Except for the first leg (which has a fixed time), the ticket is valid for **five days**. This is convenient if you need to head back early due to poor weather or plan to stay overnight on the mountain.

However, please note that if you wish to re-travel a segment you’ve already completed, you will need to purchase a new ticket.

### **Tateyama Kurobe Ticket Prices**

![2025 Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Fare Table Tateyama Kurobe Transportation Ticket](https://i0.wp.com/easytravelfollowme.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/%E6%88%AA%E5%9C%96-2025-05-04-14.15.09.png?w=2208&ssl=1)2025 Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route Fare Table｜Source: Official Website

The **top right** shows **one-way fares** for each section: **blue text for adults**, **red text for children**.

The **bottom left** shows **round-trip fares**.

To be honest, we didn’t initially expect the Alpine Route to be this expensive. However, considering these transport systems, cable cars, trolley buses, and highland buses, are built and maintained in high-altitude regions, the operating costs are understandably high, which is reflected in the price.

At 24,000 JPY, it covers unlimited rides on JR local and limited express trains (non-reserved seats) between Nagoya, Toyama, and Matsumoto for five consecutive days, plus the entire Alpine Route.

To put it in perspective, the Alpine Route ticket alone is 16,660 JPY. If you add a one-way trip from Nagoya to Toyama 10,079 JPY, the total reaches 26,739 JPY. This pass easily pays for itself, especially if your itinerary includes Toyama, Hida Takayama, Kamikochi, or Narai-juku.

## **How to Purchase the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket**

There are three main ways to buy the ticket:

1\. **On-site:** Purchase directly at the station.

2\. **Online Reservation:** Book online and collect tickets (or change times) via machines or counters on-site.

3\. **Tour Groups:** Join a guided tour where the agency handles all ticketing.

> ⚠️ **Important tip:** Every year when reservations open in March, popular slots sell out quickly. I **recommend booking online as early as possible** to secure your preferred time and avoid long waits at the ticket window.

## Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket FAQ

Do I need to book Tateyama Kurobe tickets in advance, or can I buy them on-site?

I highly recommend booking online in advance. During peak seasons like the spring Snow Wall (April to May) or autumn foliage, buying tickets on-site can take 1 to 2 hours of queuing, and popular time slots sell out fast. Reserving online secures your departure time for the first leg of the journey, ensuring a smooth itinerary.

How long is the Tateyama Kurobe ticket valid, and can I make stopovers?

The ticket is valid for 5 days. Within this period, you can make stopovers at any station along the route or even stay overnight on the mountain. However, each segment can only be traveled once in a single direction; you cannot backtrack or re-ride a section (unless you purchased a round-trip ticket from the start).

Do I need to reserve a specific time for every transportation mode on the route?

No. You only need to reserve a designated departure time for the very first leg of your journey (the cable car from Tateyama Station or the electric bus from Ogizawa Station). For all subsequent transportation modes on the route, boarding is on a first-come, first-served basis by queuing at the station.

Can I use IC cards like Suica or Pasmo on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route?

No. The entire Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route does not accept any transportation IC cards (such as Suica, Pasmo, or ICOCA). You must purchase a physical “Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route ticket” at the ticket window/machine or redeem a pre-booked online ticket before boarding.

Which JR Pass covers the entire Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route?

The most recommended pass for foreign tourists is the “ [JR Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto Area Tourist Pass](https://easytravelfollowme.com/jr-pass/alpine-takayama-matsumoto-area-en)” (priced at `* 24,000 JPY (≈ $156.00 USD / £115.44 GBP / €134.40 EUR)`). This highly cost-effective pass covers not only JR trains in Nagoya, Matsumoto, and Takayama but also provides fully covered rides on all 6 types of transportation within the Alpine Route.

# Alpine Route Tickets and How to Ride: The Complete Guide

By Dynamic Japan Travel Editorial Team—Supervised by P-HAM Co., Ltd. (Licensed Travel Agency, Aichi No. 3-1590)

Updated 28 August 2026 [Editorial policy](https://d-japantravel.com/editorial-policy)

Contents

## How to Buy Tickets and Ride the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route: The Complete Guide

The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is a mountain sightseeing route that crosses from Ogizawa on the Nagano side to Tateyama Station on the Toyama side, linking together electric buses, cable cars, a ropeway, and highland buses along the way. With so many connections, first-timers often find it hard to picture where and how to buy tickets, and what to do at each transfer — and for overseas visitors, that uncertainty tends to be the biggest worry of all.

![Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route tickets on sale at the Kippu Uriba office below snowy peaks, red tape marking the queue](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-9804fccf159affe8baabc292b87c73f3f338cbdf654162bf0173c4caa2724a09.jpg?size=1200x)Ticket counter at Ogizawa

Drawing on an actual crossing made in late November 2025, this article walks through **only how to buy tickets and how to board each ride**, one step at a time. For the highlights of the route as a whole, see the full picture of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route; for getting there from Tokyo, see how to reach the Alpine Route.

Note that the entire Alpine Route closes for the winter; it operates from spring until the end of November (exact dates vary from year to year).

Here is the bottom line up front. **If your dates are fixed, buy a WEB ticket; if you are deciding on the day, head for the ticket window at Ogizawa.** Keep your ticket on you until you exit at Tateyama Station (or Ogizawa), and send large luggage ahead with the forwarding service—stick to those two rules and the transfers go remarkably smoothly.

## First, the basics: a ticket is a combination of section, one-way or round-trip, and how you buy it

The trick to choosing without confusion is to settle these three points in order.

1\. **Where you get on and where you get off** — a through ticket covering the entire route (for example, Ogizawa to Tateyama Station), or a section ticket that stops partway (for example, as far as the Kurobe Dam).

2\. **One-way or round-trip** — one-way if you are coming out the other side, round-trip if you are returning to where you started.

3\. **When you buy** — a Web Ticket purchased online in advance, or a ticket bought on the day at the counter or a vending machine.

\| Ticket \| What it covers \| Who it suits \|

\|---\|---\|---\|

\| Through ticket, one-way \| Ogizawa to Tateyama Station, riding every connection end to end \| Anyone crossing the whole route (the standard case in this article) \|

\| Section ticket \| As far as an intermediate stop such as the Kurobe Dam or Murodo \| Visitors who only want to see the dam, or day-trippers returning the way they came \|

\| Round-trip ticket \| Out and back over the same section \| Anyone returning to a base hotel (check which sections are offered) \|

\| Web Ticket \| Bought online in advance and collected from the dedicated machine at Ogizawa \| Travelers with fixed dates who want to skip the morning queue \|

\| Same-day ticket \| Bought on the spot at the counter or a vending machine \| Travelers deciding by the weather on the day, and anyone buying a section ticket \|

## Buying a Web Ticket online in advance, step by step

On busy mornings, a queue forms at the ticket office that is separate from the line waiting to board. If your dates are already set, buying in advance is the safer bet.

**Step 1 — Buy online before you set out.** Purchase through the official online sales page, specifying your travel date and section. Be sure to check the sales window and the terms for changes and refunds at the time of purchase.

**Step 2 — Collect it on the day from the dedicated machine at Ogizawa Station.** With a Web Ticket you skip the counter queue and exchange your booking for a paper ticket at a dedicated machine. Having the confirmation details you received at purchase (such as the confirmation email) ready to show makes this quick.

![Three Web Ticket machines lined up along the building wall, with instruction signs posted above them](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-aa4029cd1d5fde13e9019eb5effa25f0060820e1576112f59b5572f399c1816d.jpg?size=1200x)Ticket machine dedicated to web tickets![Three Web Ticket machines under blue covers in the station waiting area, a ticket information sign on the wall](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-755e289a46f263b229005bb88db75f8724150c4f73155e370aa0cc9619a82063.jpg?size=1200x)Web ticket machines lined up in the waiting area

**Step 3 — Take your printed ticket to the gate.** Once you have it in hand, the rest is exactly the same as for anyone who bought on the day.

## Buying on the day, step by step

**Step 1 — Head to the ticket office.** Ogizawa Station has both a staffed ticket office and vending machines. Lines grow long around the first departure of the morning, so allow yourself plenty of time.

**Step 2 — Check the fare for your destination on the fare board.** The fare board posted near the ticket office lists one-way and round-trip fares for every station. For a through ticket, look at the row for the far end of the route — Tateyama Station if you are starting from Ogizawa.

![Route map and fare board posted inside the station, where you check the section and price before buying](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-8d0a07bb0e5ddad9c23a04dad2e94f1ad1c6bceda68581218629daaeeb60de83.jpg?size=1200x)Route map and fare table; check your section and fare here

**Step 3 — Pay.** At the counter, state your destination, whether you want one-way or round-trip, and how many people, then pay. Card acceptance may differ between counters and vending machines, so it is worth carrying a reasonable amount of cash in Japanese yen as well.

![Ticket machine screen covered in fare buttons, with handwritten notes taped around it for same-day buyers](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-0f9a1fff39895691a6cc1347edf2e8c99cb28909f07ce182e615b19571c58135.jpg?size=1200x)Ticket machines for same-day tickets; press the fare button for your destination

## How boarding works: gate, then line up, then ride

Once you have your ticket, the routine is essentially the same for every ride.

1\. **The gate** — gates open in line with the departure time. Show your ticket to a staff member (or run it through the gate machine) and head to the boarding area.

2\. **Lining up** — join the queue at the boarding area. The closer to the front you are, the more choice you have over your seat or a window spot.

3\. **Boarding** — board as directed by the staff. Rather than dashing for a departure that is about to leave, it is safer to wait for the next one.

![Ticket gates at the electric bus boarding entrance, lined with guidance signs and notices for passengers](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-a24827165553caad9bed3ab57b3060d0909289f9b0c1f5d09034492f1bb26ca2.jpg?size=1200x)Ticket gates at the electric bus boarding area![Timetable board with electric bus departures for Ogizawa and cable car runs to Kurobedaira, key to choosing a ticket](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-994750c98f028fbf66f700b6c7c55d10fec38e9e69afeabca00d160027a3144c.jpg?size=1200x)Timetable for the electric buses and cable car

**Keep hold of your ticket the whole way.** A through ticket is the same single ticket used at every transfer. The trick is to keep it somewhere you can produce it instantly each time, such as a pocket or a pass holder.

![Two travellers walking toward the ticket gate through the arched tunnel concourse of an Alpine Route station](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-57867ee2f61614d4f10f57789e98c1f159e40f238b16a1aeb75d4f58b029d5a8.jpg?size=1200x)Following the signs to the ticket gate![Two travellers waiting in line at the ticket gate inside the tunnel-shaped station building](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-82c7f81654435bc9b2819bc408351a97c85e683b95d2faca3e204d5a62c6d3f7.jpg?size=1200x)Waiting for departure in front of the ticket gate

**Luggage rules:** most of these vehicles are compact and built around their seating, so follow the rules posted on board — holding a backpack in front of you when it is crowded, for instance. Large suitcases can be difficult to bring aboard at times, so consider the **luggage forwarding service** that sends your bags ahead between Ogizawa and Tateyama Station (check drop-off points, fees, and hours). Traveling light makes the whole chain of transfers far more comfortable.

![Drop box for climbing registration forms beside a luggage notice board under the eaves of an Alpine Route station](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/studio-e5ee992f9ce0c2f779684117e34cb1508b4b93cd5c06bcc0032d2caf65f4ccce.jpg?size=1200x)Box for climbing registration forms and a notice about luggage

## Can you use the Japan Rail Pass?

**Not on the Alpine Route itself, between Ogizawa and Tateyama Station.** None of the rides on this stretch are JR lines, so they fall outside the Japan Rail Pass. The pass covers you only as far as the JR sections leading toward Ogizawa or Tateyama Station. For the full access details, see how to reach the Alpine Route.

[![Japan Rail Pass allows you unlimited travel on JR lines](https://img-v1-get.d-japantravel.com/traveltips/eyecatch-textless-20260903-japan-rail-pass.png?size=176x120)Train and Bus\\

## Ride-by-ride tips, in order from Ogizawa to Tateyama Station

- **Kanden electric bus through the Kanden Tunnel (Ogizawa to Kurobe Dam):** almost the entire ride is inside the tunnel. Rather than the view, the priority here is lining up early to secure a seat.
- **Kurobe Dam (the walking section):** not a ride as such, but a transfer leg where you walk across the top of the dam to the next station. Wear comfortable shoes.
- **Kurobe Cable Car (Kurobeko to Kurobedaira):** it runs through a tunnel, so don't count on the view; standing near the doors makes the next transfer smoother.
- **Tateyama Ropeway (Kurobedaira to Daikanbo):** the windows on the valley side, looking down on Lake Kurobe, are the best seats in the house. Line up toward the front to claim a window.
- **Tateyama Tunnel electric bus (Daikanbo to Murodo):** entirely inside a tunnel, with no views at all. Again, prioritize getting a seat.
- **Tateyama Highland Bus (Murodo to Bijodaira):** here the scenery is the main event, and the further forward you sit, the more open the view.
- **Tateyama Cable Car (Bijodaira to Tateyama Station):** the last ride of the day. The interior is stepped to match the steep gradient, so watch your footing as you get on and off.
